answer: When an agent joins, it must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake and earn access to a knoll of tasks only after completing a beacon challenge: peers issue unpredictable requests and attest to consistent responses over time. The kernel records each stake and its challenge history, so one identity cannot cheaply inherit another’s reputation. An attacker can still create many identities, but must tie up capital in each and spend real compute and time building separate histories; Sybil accounts become costly rather than merely numerous.
